blocks.content: Chandigarh's tourism chapter is dominated by planned/man-made attractions rather than natural or ancient heritage — a direct reflection of its identity as a purpose-built modern city. Expect table-based recall questions on 'which sector has which attraction'.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Rock Garden was secretly created by Nek Chand using industrial, urban, and discarded household waste.
Zakir Hussain Rose Garden is spread across 30 acres and stands as Asia's largest rose garden.
Chandigarh's Capitol Complex was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2016 under Le Corbusier's architectural works.
Sukhna Lake is a 3 sq km artificial rainfed lake created in 1958 by damming the Sukhna Choe stream.
Popular regional excursions from Chandigarh include Pinjore (Yadavindra) Gardens, Morni Hills, and the Timber Trail at Parwanoo.

cells: UNESCO World Heritage Site — Le Corbusier's High Court, Civil Secretariat, Vidhan Sabha and Open Hand Monument (see Chapter 3)
40-acre waste-material sculpture garden by self-taught artist Nek Chand Saini; one of India's most-visited man-made tourist sites, drawing millions of visitors annually
Artificial lake; Ramsar Site proposal approved 2025 (final designation pending); popular for boating, jogging track, and the annual Chandigarh Carnival
One of Asia's largest rose gardens; venue for the annual Rose Festival
City's central business district and iconic shopping/civic plaza, part of Le Corbusier's original 'heart' of the city
Le Corbusier-designed museum with Gandhara sculpture and modern-art collections
Large collection of costumed dolls from across the world
A Mughal-style terraced garden just outside Chandigarh in Panchkula district, Haryana — often visited as part of the same tourist circuit despite being outside the UT
One of North India's largest shopping malls, a major modern retail/leisure landmark
Continuous green corridor of themed gardens across sectors (see Chapter 8)

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Nek Chand's Rock Garden is regularly cited as being among the most-visited attractions in India after the Taj Mahal by some tourism-footfall rankings for man-made sites — a striking, often-quoted comparative fact (verify the latest ranking figures before quoting them in an exam answer).

rows: Sculptures created entirely from urban and industrial waste
UNESCO World Heritage seat of Punjab & Haryana governments
Asia's largest rose garden featuring over 1,600 varieties
17th-century Mughal style terraced garden outside the city

blocks.content: Nek Chand Saini, a government road inspector with no formal art training, began secretly collecting industrial and household waste — broken bangles, ceramic pieces, electrical fittings, discarded tiles — from demolished villages during Chandigarh's construction, using them to build sculptures in a forest area on government land near the Capitol Complex. His work remained illegal and unknown to authorities for nearly 18 years before being discovered in 1975; rather than demolishing it, the Chandigarh Administration chose to legitimise and formally open the Rock Garden to the public in 1976, and it has since grown into a globally recognised outsider-art environment protected by a dedicated Society (Nek Chand Foundation).

items: Nek Chand was honored with the Padma Shri in 1984 for his creation of the Rock Garden.
Capitol Complex includes three major structures: the Palace of Assembly, Secretariat, and High Court, along with the Open Hand Monument.
Morni Hills in Panchkula district is the only hill station in Haryana, situated near Chandigarh.

Pinjore Gardens (Yadavindra Gardens), Panchkula district, Haryana — a 17th-century Mughal-style terraced garden associated with the Patiala royal family's later renovations, a popular half-day trip from Chandigarh.

Kalka–Shimla Railway (a UNESCO World Heritage mountain railway) begins its journey from Kalka, easily accessible from Chandigarh, making the UT a common gateway/base for tourists heading into the Himachal hills.
Morni Hills, Haryana — the nearest hill-station-style getaway from Chandigarh, popular for short weekend trips.
Rock Garden, Sukhna Lake and the Capitol Complex — all located in Sector 1 — form Chandigarh's core tourism triangle.
Nek Chand's Rock Garden was built secretly over ~18 years (from 1957) before being discovered and legitimised in 1975–76.
Zakir Hussain Rose Garden (Sector 16) is one of Asia's largest rose gardens.
Chandigarh International Airport (Mohali) and the Kalka–Shimla Railway (UNESCO) make the city a key regional gateway.
Pinjore/Yadavindra Gardens, though outside the UT (in Haryana), is commonly bundled into the Chandigarh tourist circuit.
